clue.text: Coppers arresting a second group of politicians

indicators.note: the coppers hold the next letter inside them, as police would hold a suspect

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, so two coppers give CU twice

explanation.surface: Police officers detain someone, a second group of politicians drawn into a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police but is the chemical symbol for copper twice; 'arresting' places A inside after the first C.
explanation.definitionFit: A caucus is a closed meeting or bloc of party members, a body of politicians acting together.

clue.text: Exhausted from diving without limits

indicators.note: the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: falling is plunging downward, like a dive

explanation.surface: A diver comes out of the water utterly worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: All in is an informal phrase for completely tired out.

clue.text: Disaster unknown amongst various calm acts

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
various suggests the letters take a different form

parts.note: anagram fodder
Y is a mathematical unknown, alongside x and z

explanation.surface: A catastrophe of unknown cause strikes among various peaceful acts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amongst' places Y inside CATACLSM, the anagram of CALM ACTS from 'various'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataclysm is a sudden violent upheaval or catastrophe.

clue.text: Pigment that is kept in tin and almost overturned

indicators.note: the abbreviation is held inside the tin symbol

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
ie is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

indicators.note: in a down entry the shortened word is turned upside down
the last letter is cut off the word

explanation.surface: Paint pigment stored in a tin which has nearly toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts AND to AN, and 'overturned' gives NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth pigment, brownish-yellow raw or reddish-brown burnt.

clue.text: 'Single maiden should go around clubs' is the wrong thing to say

indicators.note: the single maiden wraps itself about the following letters

parts.note: sole means single or only
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice that an unmarried woman should tour the nightclubs, quoted as something tactless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' looks like nightclubs but is the card suit; the single maiden splits to hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a grammatical blunder or breach of etiquette, an error in speech.

clue.text: It answers query with third of riders misbehaving

definitions.text: It answers query with third of riders misbehaving

indicators.note: letters that misbehave are out of order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: the third letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: In horse racing, an investigation looks into whether jockeys broke the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes all of IT ANSWERS QUERY plus D. The whole clue is also the definition: race officials hold this inquiry when riders may have misbehaved.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing the officials hold this hearing into possible rule breaking by jockeys during a race.

clue.text: Radio report mentioning actual coastline

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: literal means actual, exact rather than figurative

explanation.surface: A radio bulletin describing the real coastline.
explanation.definitionFit: The littoral is the shore region of a sea or lake.

clue.text: Court accepting airmen will display skill

indicators.note: the court's letters take in the airmen

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: A court that admits pilots will show their ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft is skill or expertise in making or doing something.

clue.text: Special redesign of raiment for a fresh taste …

indicators.note: the clothing word is rearranged as if remade

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A special remodelling of clothes is offered for a new style, the ellipsis linking to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a common mint flavour, prized for its refreshing taste.

clue.text: Good wishes given by every expert?

parts.note: all can stand for every one of a group
an expert is among the top performers, the finest at something

explanation.surface: Kind regards offered by each specialist in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'expert' stands loosely for the top people in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a common farewell or toast expressing hope for someone's success.

clue.text: Top copy having indication of mistake

parts.note: to ape is to imitate or copy
a cross is the mark a teacher puts by an error

explanation.surface: A top copy of a document carries a mark showing an error.
explanation.definitionFit: An apex is the highest point or summit of something.

clue.text: Snake in study died, covered by three articles

indicators.note: the articles sit around the study and died pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: the articles an, a and a joined together
to con is to study or learn by heart
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A snake appears in someone's study and dies, its death reported in three newspaper articles.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a very large South American constrictor.

clue.text: Protest, being on strike with regular appearances from Corbyn

parts.note: workers who are out have stopped work in a strike

indicators.note: every other letter of the name is taken, starting with its first

explanation.surface: A walkout protest that Jeremy Corbyn, the former Labour leader, keeps visiting.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcry is a strong public protest or clamour of objection.

clue.text: Remain lost, losing heart

indicators.note: the central letter of the five-letter word is dropped

parts.note: a stray animal is one that is lost

explanation.surface: Someone stays put, feeling lost and dispirited.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain in a place or condition.

clue.text: … note redesign of raiment and stop

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the clothing word is rearranged as if remade

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: a memo ordering the clothes redesign to be halted.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate is to end or bring to a halt.

clue.text: Sudden return of detectives, apprehending scoundrel imprisoning mother

indicators.note: the detectives hold the scoundrel inside them, as an arrest would
the detectives' letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

indicators.note: the scoundrel shuts the mother inside

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Detectives make a swift return to catch a villain who has locked up his mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' reverses the detectives to give DIC, which holds the scoundrel-and-mother piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatic change is one that is abrupt and striking, so the adjective means sudden.

clue.text: A failure to retain speed — right? — implied encumbrance

indicators.note: the failure holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a loss is a failure or defeat
bat means speed or pace, as in going at a fair bat

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about failing to keep up speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bat for speed is British slang, as in 'at a fair old bat'. The definition is figurative: the burden is only implied.
explanation.definitionFit: From Coleridge's Ancient Mariner, an albatross is a burden of guilt one cannot shake off.

clue.text: Be understudy to lead in Caesar — done with a lot of class

indicators.note: the leading letter of the name is taken

parts.note: over means finished or done

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a form is a school class

explanation.surface: Standing in for the lead in Julius Caesar, with plenty of class.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover for someone is to stand in and do their job in their absence.

clue.text: Flower border captured in writing

indicators.note: the border is enclosed by the writing

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A flowered border is described in a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring flower of woods and hedges.

clue.text: Group avoiding cold dip

indicators.note: the group's letters go without the cold one

parts.note: a batch is a set or group of things
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A group of swimmers skip the chilly plunge.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath is a soak or dip in water.

clue.text: Food container from Berlin perhaps with two bits swapped

indicators.note: the two halves of the word change places

parts.note: Berlin is an example of something German, being the German capital

explanation.surface: A lunchbox from Berlin with two parts switched around.
explanation.definitionFit: A manger is a trough from which livestock eat.

clue.text: One bad deed leading to a lot of fun

indicators.note: the bad deed comes first, before the fun

parts.note: a sin is a wrongful act

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: glee is merriment or fun

explanation.surface: A single misdeed that sets off a lot of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Single means one only, a unit rather than a pair or more.

clue.text: Rise, having adopted Republican party

indicators.note: the rise phrase takes the letter into itself

parts.note: to go up is to rise

explanation.surface: A party gains ground after taking on a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: A group is a party of people gathered or classed together.

clue.text: Put figure on new source of trade if investing in wharf

indicators.note: the pieces go into the wharf, putting money into it

parts.note: a quay is a landing wharf

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to estimate what a new trading source would bring if funds were put into a wharf.
explanation.definitionFit: To quantify is to express something as a number or measure it.

clue.text: The French provided upset surrounding northern match

indicators.note: the reversed letters go around the next one
in a down entry the pieces are turned upside down

parts.note: la is the feminine form of the in French
if means provided that

explanation.surface: French fans, upset, gather around a northern team's match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LAIF into FIAL, split by N.
explanation.definitionFit: A final is the deciding match of a competition.

clue.text: Helping of ragout — a colourful exotic food

indicators.note: Helping of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A serving of bright stew is offered as something foreign to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A taco is a Mexican folded tortilla with filling, foreign fare to a British solver.

clue.text: Reasonable justification for entertainment centre

parts.note: fair means reasonable or just
a ground is a reason or justification, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: A fair reason is offered for building a leisure venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground is an outdoor site with rides and stalls, a place for amusement.

clue.text: Final gathering in support of would-be union member

definitions.text: Final gathering in support of would-be union member

parts.words: Final gathering in support of would-be union member
parts.note: the 'union' is a marriage, and the would-be member is a bride enjoying a last party with friends before her wedding

explanation.walkthrough: 'union member' suggests a trade unionist; the union is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: This celebration for a bride-to-be with her women friends marks the end of single life.

clue.text: Take stock, with stone being thrown into convention

indicators.note: the stone is tossed inside the convention's letters

parts.note: a rule is a convention or standard practice
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A stone is hurled into a conference while someone reviews their inventory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take stock' looks like doing an inventory; it means stealing livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: To rustle is to steal cattle or horses, carrying off livestock.
